title: Boss: follow the packet
summary: From a URL to a pod IP, through the Gateway, DNS and Service.

steps.title: The scene
steps.body: A request arrives at `https://shop.example.com/api/cart`. It passes the Gateway, a Service, and lands on a pod. Each hop can fail in its own way. Build the pieces of a tool that traces the path.

steps.title: Trace a request
prompt: Write `string Trace(string host, string path, List<(string Host, string Prefix, string Service)> rules, Dictionary<string, List<string>> endpoints)`:

- pick the rule with an exactly matching host and the longest matching prefix (segment rules as in *Route a request*: equal, or followed by `/`, and `/` matches everything; ignore any-host rules here). None: `"404 no rule"`.
- look up the Service in `endpoints`. Missing or empty: `"503 <service> has no endpoints"`.
starter: string Trace(string host, string path, List<(string Host, string Prefix, string Service)> rules, Dictionary<string, List<string>> endpoints)
solution: string Trace(string host, string path, List<(string Host, string Prefix, string Service)> rules, Dictionary<string, List<string>> endpoints)
var rule = rules.Where(r => r.Host == host && PrefixMatch(r.Prefix, path))
if (!endpoints.TryGetValue(svc, out var eps) || eps.Count == 0) return $"503 {svc} has no endpoints";
template: var dojoRules = new List<(string Host, string Prefix, string Service)> { ("shop.example.com", "/", "web"), ("shop.example.com", "/api", "api"), ("shop.example.com", "/admin", "admin") };
var dojoEps = new Dictionary<string, List<string>> { ["web"] = new() { "10.1.0.4:3000" }, ["api"] = new() { "10.1.0.9:8080", "10.1.1.2:8080" }, ["admin"] = new() };
Dojo.Eq("admin has no endpoints", "503 admin has no endpoints", Trace("shop.example.com", "/admin", dojoRules, dojoEps));
Dojo.Eq("unknown host", "404 no rule", Trace("x.example.com", "/", dojoRules, dojoEps));
Dojo.Eq("missing service entry", "503 api has no endpoints", Trace("shop.example.com", "/api", dojoRules, new Dictionary<string, List<string>>()));

steps.title: Spread requests round-robin
steps.prompt: kube-proxy in IPVS mode can spread connections round-robin. Write `Dictionary<string, int> Spread(List<string> endpoints, int requests)` returning how many requests each endpoint receives when they are handed out in turn, starting with the first. Every endpoint appears in the result, even with 0.
starter: Dictionary<string, int> Spread(List<string> endpoints, int requests)
solution: Dictionary<string, int> Spread(List<string> endpoints, int requests)
for (int i = 0; i < requests; i++) counts[endpoints[i % endpoints.Count]]++;

steps.title: Diagnose a connection
prompt: Put the checks in the order an engineer would. Write `string Diagnose(bool dnsResolves, int endpointCount, bool targetPortMatchesApp, bool policyAllows)` returning the **first** problem found:
1. `"dns: name does not resolve (check namespace and spelling)"`
4. `"port: targetPort does not match the port the app listens on"`
starter: string Diagnose(bool dnsResolves, int endpointCount, bool targetPortMatchesApp, bool policyAllows)
solution: string Diagnose(bool dnsResolves, int endpointCount, bool targetPortMatchesApp, bool policyAllows)
if (!dnsResolves) return "dns: name does not resolve (check namespace and spelling)";
if (endpointCount == 0) return "endpoints: selector matches no ready pods";
if (!policyAllows) return "policy: a NetworkPolicy blocks the traffic";
if (!targetPortMatchesApp) return "port: targetPort does not match the port the app listens on";
template: Dojo.Eq("dns first", "dns: name does not resolve (check namespace and spelling)", Diagnose(false, 0, false, false));
Dojo.Eq("no endpoints", "endpoints: selector matches no ready pods", Diagnose(true, 0, false, false));
Dojo.Eq("policy before port", "policy: a NetworkPolicy blocks the traffic", Diagnose(true, 2, false, false));
Dojo.Eq("wrong port", "port: targetPort does not match the port the app listens on", Diagnose(true, 2, false, true));
hints: A chain of `if` statements, one per check, in the listed order.
